title: The Zenos, Charlie McCurdy and piccolo in the Peerless band
summary: Possible Zeno family links, Charlie McCurdy on clarinet, and piccolo player Bab Frank in the Peerless band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: It was a drummer, wasn't there, Zeno? Henry Zeno. I wonder if she was any relation to him.
They had a couple of Zenos around here. I usually call his mother Mrs. Lewis, but her real name is Mrs. Zeno, Alice Zeno. He might be a part.

There might be some relation. There might be some relation. There might be a part. I'm telling you. Jerry don't talk much, you know. Oh, did you ever hear Charlie McCurdy much? How was he on clarinet? Well, he was great. You know, he was playing nothing but strictly music, you know, and make all kinds of sweet – really harmonious stuff. He was good. Who did he play with? Do you know?
Oh, he played with all them bands.
All the bands. All the bands. All the bands. The last band they had to meet up, they had the Peerless band. Peerless, yeah.
Oh, he played piccolo, didn't he?
Yeah, he left them, yeah. He never come back. That old boy's prison piccolo though. Bab Frank.
What kind of a part did they play in the band? You played piccolo too, you said.
Yeah, playing things like a clarinet. Just like clarinet.
Yeah, I think it would be good in the band.
They play a piccolo inside with the band or is that strictly for a parade in the way? Inside of the band.

Inside of the band. For dancing? Dancing. Inside of the band. I mean, I've made a piccolo player, you know. Players, I mean, like that. That's Frank and all that kind of. That's the only one I know, that's Frank. I knew he could make that thing talk. And he played just quite a bit like a clarinet. Played like a clarinet, played a clarinet, all those different things. You had a rascal man who'd look like he wouldn't be playing but he's playing. Well, that's really sounding like something. It's good all right.
